claims.text: A thin CrN layer inserted between elemental Cr and the zirconium-alloy substrate will inhibit elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Inhibiting Cr–Zr interdiffusion with the CrN layer will prevent premature coating failure.
The CrN-modified coating will preserve corrosion protection during normal subcritical-water operation.
The CrN-modified coating will preserve corrosion protection during accident-relevant high-temperature steam exposure.
The proposed intervention is deposition of a conformal CrN layer tens of nanometers thick on the zirconium alloy before deposition of elemental Cr.
Approximately 300°C subcritical water represents the normal-operation test regime.
Approximately 1000°C steam represents an accident-relevant transient test regime.
CrN has sufficiently low diffusivity to act as a physical barrier to intermixing of Cr and Zr at the coating–substrate interface.
Cr–Zr interdiffusion produces deleterious Cr–Zr intermetallic compounds that weaken the coating.
Impeding atomic diffusion with CrN will suppress formation of deleterious Cr–Zr intermetallic compounds.
The CrN barrier will maintain distinct Cr, CrN, and zirconium-alloy layers under both normal-operation and accident conditions.
Relative to the unmodified Cr-coated baseline, CrN-barrier samples will have a thinner interdiffusion zone.
Relative to the unmodified baseline, CrN-barrier samples will retain better coating integrity.
Relative to the unmodified baseline, CrN-barrier samples will exhibit superior corrosion resistance in subcritical water and short-term high-temperature steam.
An elemental Cr coating without a diffusion barrier undergoes premature high-temperature failure due to Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The optimal CrN thickness and its long-term stability under reactor-specific irradiation and stress are undetermined.
Incomplete interfacial coverage may limit the effectiveness of the CrN barrier.
Equivalent or worse interdiffusion thickness, coating degradation, or corrosion rate in CrN-barrier samples under either test regime would falsify the hypothesis.
